facts.text: Terézváros is District VI of Budapest, named after Queen Maria Theresa who visited in 1751 and officially named the area in 1777.
The Hungarian State Opera House, opened in 1884, sits on Andrássy Avenue, a UNESCO World Heritage boulevard that defines the district’s cultural heart.
The district’s early 18th‑century development pushed people beyond Pest’s old town, making Terézváros the first planned extension of the city.
Andrássy Avenue’s 1896 wood trim and cream tiles remain visible at the Opera and Bajcsy‑Zsilinszky stations, echoing the district’s historic transit era.
Terézváros hosts the Franz Liszt Academy of Music, a renowned music academy whose restored façade attracts students and visitors alike.
